elements.quote: Models for malaria control optimization-a systematic review
elements.reason: The document title explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: Models for malaria control optimization-a systematic review
elements.reason: The title provides key information about the population (malaria) and intervention/exposure (control optimization).
The review is not identified as a living review or update, so supplementary information regarding update status is not applicable.

elements.quote: Despite advances made in curbing the global malaria burden since the 2000s, progress has stalled, in part due to a plateauing of the financing available to implement needed interventions.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the current state of knowledge (stalled progress) and uncertainties (financing gap) regarding malaria control.

elements.quote: There is a dire need to carry out more representative and country-specific modelling studies for resource allocation across Africa and the Asia Pacific, for malaria control or elimination.
elements.reason: The text explicitly explains the importance and need for the review by highlighting the dire need for more representative modelling studies.
The provided text does not mention any previous systematic reviews on this topic to justify the current review as an update or replication.
The text lists interventions but does not describe the proposed mechanism of action of the interventions in the rationale section.
The provided text does not mention a logic model to show hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes.

elements.quote: The research question for this review was ' Are there English-language publications in peer-reviewed scientific journals describing how models have been used to allocate resources for malaria interventions in limited resource settings?'
elements.reason: The review explicitly states its research question in the Search Strategy section.

elements.quote: A systematic literature review is presented here, to identify available models for malaria control optimization for resource allocation in limited resource settings, determine how they have been used and to assess them for quality and utility.
elements.reason: The review aims to characterize optimization models rather than compare intervention effects directly, making PICO comparisons of intervention effects not applicable.

elements.quote: Each record in the search were included if they met all of the following criteria: (1) Were scientific peer-reviewed journals written in English; (2) Were published before 30th June 2024; (3) Studies were included irrespective of the targeted geographical regions; (4) Studies were included irrespective of the population subgroups; (5) Studies containing an optimization model (mathematical or statistical); (6) All studies with human Plasmodium species; (7) Studies with two or more interventions; (8) Cost data were used in combination with the model outputs; (9) Outcomes/health benefits were clearly stated and/or measured.
elements.reason: Specifies study designs, settings, and populations, but does not explicitly specify follow-up requirements.

elements.quote: Each record in the search were included if they met all of the following criteria: (1) Were scientific peer-reviewed journals written in English; (2) Were published before 30th June 2024; ... The following records were excluded: (1) Editorials, commentaries, opinion papers, conference abstracts, media reports, letters, bulletins, pre-prints, grey literature; (2) Non-English language studies; (3) Systematic reviews, meta-analyses.
elements.reason: Explicitly specifies language, dissemination year, and publication/report status in inclusion and exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: Full text articles excluded: 66 No optimisation model, 24 Conference abstracts, 8 Reviews, 6 One intervention only, 5 Non-human population, 3 Preprints
elements.reason: The text does not distinguish between exclusion because outcomes were not measured versus outcomes not reported.

elements.quote: A narrative synthesis of the study characteristics was performed.

elements.quote: Of the twelve studies that used dynamic transmission models in combination with economic/cost models for optimization, six (40.0%) used compartmental models... and the other six (40.0%) used individual-based models... elements.quote: There is a marked heterogeneity across all studies... disparities in these optimization modelling analyses across studies make the comparison of the methods used to measure outcomes across these studies difficult.
elements.reason: No subgroup analysis or meta-regression was performed; the review acknowledges heterogeneity but states it makes comparison difficult.

elements.quote: There is a marked heterogeneity across all studies... disparities in these optimization modelling analyses across studies make the comparison of the methods used to measure outcomes across these studies difficult.
elements.reason: No subgroup analysis or meta-regression was performed, so reporting on study-level variables or within-study contrasts is not applicable.

elements.quote: There is a marked heterogeneity across all studies... disparities in these optimization modelling analyses across studies make the comparison of the methods used to measure outcomes across these studies difficult.
elements.reason: No analyses of heterogeneity were performed or described, so identifying non-pre-specified analyses is not applicable.
The Data Extraction And Synthesis section describes the narrative synthesis performed but does not report any sensitivity analyses conducted to assess the robustness of the synthesised results.
As no sensitivity analyses are reported in the manuscript, there is no information identifying whether any were pre-specified or not.

elements.quote: A full summary of all included articles can be found in Table 3.
elements.reason: The text explicitly states that a full summary of all included articles is available in Table 3, and specific reference numbers are cited throughout the results section (e.g., [10, 11, 16-18...]), indicating all studies are cited.

elements.quote: A full summary of all included articles can be found in Table 3.
elements.reason: The text confirms that key characteristics of included studies are summarized in Table 3, satisfying the requirement to present characteristics in a table.

The review focuses on characterizing models for malaria control optimization rather than evaluating intervention effects directly. The research question targets 'how models have been used', making the specific requirement for intervention details in an additional table (typical for intervention reviews) not applicable.

elements.quote: Regarding the quality of the studies included in this review, all the studies included the statement of decision problem, the statement of modelling objective, describing health and other outcomes, labelling and describing parameters and initial values, describing cost inputs and transmission dynamics (Fig. 3).
elements.reason: The manuscript presents aggregate quality assessment data (Figure 3) showing proportions of studies meeting criteria, but does not provide a table or figure listing domain-level and overall risk-of-bias (quality) judgements for every included study individually.

elements.quote: The quality of all included studies was assessed using the joint International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research-Society for Medical Decision Making Modelling Good Research Practices Task Force (ISPOR) [19].
elements.reason: Justifications for risk-of-bias judgements for individual studies are not presented in the retrieved evidence; only the criteria used are mentioned.
No evidence of outcome-specific risk-of-bias judgements displayed alongside study results was found in the retrieved text or images.
The review reports aggregate frequencies of study characteristics (e.g., Table 2) rather than summary statistics for each group for every outcome per study.
No effect estimates or measures of precision (e.g., confidence intervals) are reported as the review characterizes models rather than pooling clinical outcomes.
Visual results (e.g., Fig 2, Fig 3) are not accompanied by a corresponding tabular display in the retrieved evidence; Table 2 aggregates data rather than listing individual study results.

elements.quote: The databases PubMed and Embase (OVID) were searched... 1 article from bibliography were included
elements.reason: Multiple data sources for study identification (PubMed, Embase, Bibliography) are explicitly reported in the search strategy and results sections.
The text mentions querying authors for missing data but does not explicitly identify which results were computed or estimated in the final reporting.

elements.reason: The manuscript reports quality assessment of studies using ISPOR criteria (text_8, text_10) but does not report overall certainty or confidence levels for the body of evidence for each outcome.
No reasons for rating certainty down or up are explained, as no certainty ratings are reported.
Certainty is not communicated in the results or discussion sections using a section-appropriate format.
No GRADE Summary of Findings tables or similar evidence summary tables are included in the retrieved evidence (text_10 mentions Table 3 but does not describe it as a certainty table).

elements.quote: However, the review has certain limitations, which are outlined below: The review did not include abstracts from scientific conferences or other scientific meetings, potentially omitting important modelling studies conducted by national malaria control programs (NMCPs) to inform resource allocation decisions.
elements.reason: The text explicitly identifies limitations of the review process, such as the exclusion of conference abstracts.

elements.quote: The absence of these studies from the review limits the comprehensiveness of the findings, suggesting a need for the development of additional approaches to better capture and reflect the full range of modelling activities being undertaken globally.
elements.reason: The text discusses the potential impact of the limitations, noting that the absence of certain studies limits the comprehensiveness of the findings.

elements.quote: The findings highlighted the need for country-specific modelling analysis for malaria control optimization, country-specific epidemiological and cost data for analysis, performing cost sensitivity analyses and defining the perspective for the analysis, with an emphasis on subnational tailoring for data collection and analysis for more accurate and good quality results. Such efforts should include all efficient prevention and treatment interventions, and surveillance and vaccination to inform context-specific control and elimination efforts respectively.
elements.reason: The conclusion section explicitly discusses the need for specific modeling approaches and intervention types, addressing implications for practice.

elements.quote: Efforts towards developing publicly available applications of the models and sharing source codes to facilitate translation for policy engagement will enhance transparency, reproducibility and adaptability, and pave a way towards more harmonized models for malaria control optimization in the future.
elements.reason: The text explicitly mentions facilitating translation for policy engagement, addressing policy implications.

elements.quote: It is critical that the future modelling efforts account for equity considerations and target at risk malaria populations that are hard-to-reach to maximize impact.
elements.reason: The text provides explicit recommendations for future modeling efforts regarding equity and target populations.

elements.quote: The protocol for the systematic review was registered with the international Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) with the registration number CRD42023436966.
elements.reason: The Methods section explicitly states the register name (PROSPERO) and the registration number (CRD42023436966), fulfilling the requirement to provide registration information.
